title: 3 Bed · 2.5 Bath 2-Story Modern Scandinavian Residence
designer_rationale: The Central Circulation Spine scheme balances a high circulation score (95) with perfect privacy and daylight performance. Its linear foyer and hallway create a clear, intuitive path between public entertaining zones and rear private suites, reducing wayfinding complexity while preserving acoustic separation. The layout maximizes daylight from the south façade across both public and private spaces and maintains a tight spatial efficiency (96.1). Compared to the Public‑Private Split, its superior circulation outweighs the marginal difference in overall score. Site-first planning with South frontage, 5.0ft front setback, and 3 bedrooms across 1192.8 sq ft.

construction_spec.reason: RCC framed structure recommended for 2-story residential building with span flexibility and seismic resilience.
assumptions: External perimeter walls configured as 9.0" (229mm) masonry for weatherproofing.
Internal partition walls configured as 4.5" (114mm) space-saving masonry.
Floor-to-floor vertical rise of 10.5' provides 9.5' clear head room after MEP/false ceiling drops.
Reinforced concrete slab assumed at 5.5" thickness with grade M20/M25 concrete.
Quality standard tier: Standard finishes and construction tolerances.

strengths: Excellent circulation (95) with a single, well‑defined spine
Full privacy (100) and daylight (100) for all zones
Efficient use of floor area (96.1) and strong furniture fit (94.4)
Clear hierarchy of public to private spaces
weaknesses: Potential bottleneck at the central foyer if traffic peaks
Limited flexibility for future re‑programming of interior walls
suggestions: Introduce a secondary side pocket door to relieve foyer congestion
Provide a modest secondary circulation loop for service access
Consider sliding partitions in the public zone to increase spatial adaptability
